calibration.method: Platt (sigmoid) on raw margin, fit on train out-of-fold scores

config_history.content: Rule A only. Written by the same run that first produced validation results; the rule itself had been specified in the approved proposal beforehand.
Rule A replaced by Rule B after validation results (user decision D-09); validation-informed
Both rules retained with the roles above (user decision D-10). Models, calibration, features, splits, seeds and parameters unchanged from v1 and v2.

cost_definition: total = c * (number flagged, true or false alerts) + sum(Amount of every missed, unflagged fraud)

costs.currency: EUR (matches dataset Amount); ALL VALUES HYPOTHETICAL, not PayGuard operating costs

assumptions: constant review cost c per flagged transaction (hypothetical)
a flagged fraud is fully prevented (loss avoided = Amount)
rule_A.known_limits_from_validation: Calibration had only been checked in aggregate. A later validation-only diagnostic (outputs/m2_validation_amount_band_calibration.json) showed over-prediction in Amount bands above EUR 10, which p*Amount amplifies. At c=5 it cost XGBoost EUR 1,726 on validation vs ~EUR 630 for in-sample reference cutoffs.
rule_A.role: Original decision rule, specified in the approved M2 proposal before any Stage 2a result was computed (the v1 config file itself was written by the same run that first computed validation results). Primary comparator.

assumptions: every missed fraud costs the TRAIN mean fraud Amount (real fraud sizes are highly skewed)
a flagged fraud is fully prevented
rule_B.claim: No claim of theoretical superiority over Rule A; Rule A is the principled rule under its own assumptions.
rule_B.known_limits: Cannot distinguish a small from a large transaction at equal p; depends entirely on the hypothetical c and on a mean from 2013 European data; at low c its threshold sits where calibration is weakest.
rule_B.role: Validation-informed, secondary operating-policy alternative. NOT independently pre-registered. An AVERAGE-LOSS APPROXIMATION, not a transaction-specific expected-cost calculation: it treats every missed fraud as costing the same constant amount.

decision_rules.test_protocol: Both rules are deterministic functions of the frozen scores and are evaluated on the test set once; neither is chosen using test results.

xgboost.scale_pos_weight: negatives/positives of the training data it is fit on

preprocessing.logreg: StandardScaler fit on the data passed to fit (train only) inside a Pipeline

split.rule: sort by Time (stable); cut at Time values found at 70% and 85% row positions; ties go to the later split
split.test: not accessed during Stage 2a (only its start time is read from the Time column)
